# brewpage-openapi

Public contract snapshots, documentation and the BrewPage MCP server. The backend-generated public JSON contract is authoritative; this repository distributes deterministic copies.

## What's here

- `openapi/openapi.json` — exported backend-generated public OpenAPI 3.1 contract; version and provenance identify the backend source.
- `openapi/openapi.yaml` — deterministic derived representation; `docs/public/openapi.json` is the identical Scalar copy.
- `mcp-server/` — TypeScript implementation of the BrewPage MCP server. Prepared `version: 1.12.1`. Published as `brewpage-mcp` on npm.
- `docs/` — Astro docs site published at https://kochetkov-ma.github.io/brewpage-openapi/.

## Where to read the live API

- Spec (browser-rendered): https://kochetkov-ma.github.io/brewpage-openapi/api-reference/
- Spec (raw JSON): https://kochetkov-ma.github.io/brewpage-openapi/openapi.json
- Spec (raw YAML): https://raw.githubusercontent.com/kochetkov-ma/brewpage-openapi/main/openapi/openapi.yaml
- Live `/v3/api-docs` from production backend: https://brewpage.app/v3/api-docs
- `llms.txt`: https://brewpage.app/llms.txt
- `llms-full.txt`: https://brewpage.app/llms-full.txt

## Recent contract changes

- 1.135.0 (matches backend v1.135.0): `POST /api/html`, `PUT /api/html/{ns}/{id}` and public `.html` via `POST /api/files` repair a chat-pasted `html` page: wrapping ```` ```html ```` fence or chat text removed (notice `chat-text-removed`), entity-escaped page restored (notice `escaped-html-restored`); new query `verbatim=true` stores bytes as sent; `/source` returns the stored text. 33 paths and 47 operations.
- 1.134.0 (matches backend v1.134.0): `POST /api/files` publishes a UTF-8 `.html`/`.htm` file in `public` without a password as an HTML page (same rules as `POST /api/html`; `id`/`link`/`ownerLink` = the page, manage via `/api/html`, notice `html-file-as-page`; GET -> `308` `/api/html/public/{id}`; DELETE removes the page); other HTML files stay source (notice `html-file-as-source`); content already published by another owner -> that page, `X-Existing-Resource: 1`, notice `existing-page-not-owned` (token cannot manage it). `403` `Upload refused` on `POST /api/files`, `/api/html`, `/api/sites`; PUT html/sites 403 = missing or wrong owner token, or upload refused. Raw `xml` page reads -> `text/plain`, downloads keep `text/xml`. Site `entry` must be `.html`/`.htm`, else the default entry with a notice. 33 paths and 47 operations.
- 1.133.0 (matches backend v1.133.0): `GET /api/gallery` descriptions match behavior: `q` searches titles (filename for files, id when untitled), not tags; `mine=true` + `X-Owner-Token` lists the caller's live pages, files and sites in any namespace incl. password-protected, each with `namespace` and `visibility` (my_public, my_public_password, my_private); no token -> empty page. `GalleryItem.type` = page format (`html`, `markdown`, code format), `file` or `site`; KV/JSON stores never listed. Description-only: 33 paths and 47 operations.
- 1.132.0 (matches backend v1.132.0): `POST /api/reports` documents `429` with `ErrorResponse` when an address sends too many reports in a day; retry after the `Retry-After` header. No other change: 33 paths and 47 operations.
- 1.130.0 (matches backend v1.130.0): `info.description` links the comparison hub https://brewpage.app/compare (BrewPage vs GitHub Pages, GitHub Gist, Netlify Drop, Cloudflare Drop, Tiiny Host, Static.app). No path, operation or schema change: 33 paths and 47 operations. MCP 1.12.1 links it from its README.
- 1.125.1 (matches backend v1.125.1): `POST /api/html` JSON body (`HtmlUploadRequest`) accepts optional `format`, which wins over `?format=`; `PUT` ignores a blank body `format`; a JSON object body without `content` is published raw with a `body-as-content` notice instead of 400. 33 paths and 47 operations.
- 1.123.0 (matches backend v1.123.0): new `GET /api/limits` (`getLimits`) returns user-facing upload limits in bytes (`requestMaxBytes`; `sites.maxFiles`, `maxFileBytes`, `maxTotalBytes`, `maxArchiveExpansionBytes`, `maxPathChars`, `maxPathBytes`, `maxNameBytes`, `defaultTtlDays`, `maxTtlDays`, `allowedExtensions`, `skippedFileNames`, `skippedRootFolders`). Sites hold 200 files (was 100). Site uploads: 400 for a site limit hit (message names it), a bad ZIP or a `..` path; 413 for a request over 25 MB, too many parts or an overlong file name/path; 422 (was 415) when no servable file is left. Unstorable metadata answers 400 instead of 409. 33 paths and 47 operations. MCP 1.12.0 adds `get_limits`.
- 1.121.0 (matches backend v1.121.0): `GET /galleries` is paginated with `rel=prev/next` via an optional 1-based `page` query parameter (omitted = page 1); an invalid or past-the-end page answers 404. 32 paths and 46 operations.
- 1.119.0 (matches backend v1.119.0): publish endpoints accept fixable inputs and return an advisory `notices` array of `{code, message}` on successful create/update responses (TTL units and clamping, format aliases, skipped site members, file type sniffing, namespace normalisation, empty password, blank owner token). 32 paths and 46 operations; always use the returned `link`.
- 1.118.0 (matches backend v1.118.0): delivery-mode and hosting-version mismatches are reported, not rejected. An explicit `path` where `subdomain` is required publishes on the subdomain; a stale `expectedVersion` still applies; locked modes and OLD links answer 200 unchanged; `X-Delivery-Mode` on content updates is ignored. Such responses carry `deliveryModeMatched: false`, `deliveryModeReason` (`policy:<code>`) and `deliveryNotice`, now also on `HostingProjection`. `expectedVersion` is optional; `409 HOSTING_VERSION_CONFLICT`, `HOSTING_MODE_LOCKED`, `DELIVERY_MODE_REQUIRED` and `HOSTING_OPERATION_REQUIRED`/`HOSTING_UPDATE_REQUIRED` are gone. `POST /api/files` accepts any single file part when `file` is absent. 32 paths and 46 operations; always use the returned `link`.
- 1.117.0 (matches backend v1.117.0): NEW sites and non-public HTML pages of format `html` require `subdomain` (explicit `path` answers 400 `DELIVERY_MODE_REQUIRED`); everything else in non-public namespaces (Markdown, code/text, files, JSON, KV) defaults to `path` like public and may choose `subdomain` via `X-Delivery-Mode`. Markdown raw HTML is rendered through an allowlist (no scripts, styles, event handlers, forms or embeds; links `http`/`https`/`mailto`/`tel`/relative). Earlier pages change only when republished. 32 paths and 46 operations; always use the returned `link`.
- 1.113.0 (matches backend v1.113.0): the `result` outcome schema is named `PublicationResult`; fields, values and response bodies are unchanged (`merged` = an existing publication was returned). `POST /api/files` answers `X-Existing-Resource: 1` when it returns an existing upload. 32 paths and 46 operations.
- 1.108.0 (matches backend v1.108.0): `GET /preview/{ns}/{id}.jpg` (`previewJpeg`) is the canonical 1200×630 JPEG social preview image; `GET /preview/{ns}/{id}.png` (`preview`) remains a legacy URL serving the same JPEG bytes. Non-public or protected images carry `X-Robots-Tag: noindex`; failures redirect to `/og-image.png?v=3`. One shared `preview` tag; 32 paths and 46 operations.
- 1.107.6 (matches backend v1.107.6): contract metadata only. `info.license` is `Apache-2.0` (`https://www.apache.org/licenses/LICENSE-2.0`); paths, operations and schemas are the same as in 1.107.4.
- 1.107.4 (matches backend v1.107.4): contract metadata only. `info.termsOfService`, `info.contact` and top-level `externalDocs` are present again; paths, operations and schemas are the same as in 1.107.2, the first backend-generated snapshot.
- 1.104.0 (matches backend v1.104.0): `POST /api/html` and `PUT /api/html/{ns}/{id}` responses may carry optional `deliveryModeReason` (`auto:<codes>` or `advisory:<codes>`) and `deliveryNotice`, plus `visibilityNotice`. A public page created without `X-Delivery-Mode` may be published on its own subdomain when it needs browser features a BrewPage link does not provide; always use the returned `link`. A repost of already-published content returns the existing page with `200` and `X-Existing-Resource: 1`. `PUT` accepts an optional `format`.
- 1.31.0 (matches backend v1.41.0): `POST /api/html` and `PUT /api/html/{ns}/{id}` accept raw `text/*` and (POST only) `application/octet-stream` bodies. Binary payloads route to `/api/files`. New 422 response with `supportedTypes` array; 415 enriched. See `https://brewpage.app/llms-full.txt`.

## How to use the MCP server

```bash
npx -y brewpage-mcp@1.12.1
```

Always pin an exact version.

The server wraps a subset of REST operations in seventeen tools — read `mcp-server/README.md` for supported inputs and tool list. Omitted REST namespace defaults to `public`; omitted MCP namespace generates an unlisted `priv-*` namespace. Unlisted is readable by anyone with the link unless password-protected. Use explicit `public` only for gallery/search eligibility; protected publications are excluded and unlisted, protected or otherwise ineligible native responses are search-excluded; eligible public HTML, sites and files may permit indexing.

Use the exact returned primary `link`, including root slashes. Send API passwords as `X-Password` and owner authority as `X-Owner-Token` to the configured apex API origin; never send owner tokens to publication hosts. NEW browser password access uses the trusted unlock gateway, without query-password links. HTML API reads return stored rendered HTML or code/text with format-specific MIME; the owner-only source endpoint returns original authored content. Share URLs may provide a viewer.

Default repository limits: HTML 5 MiB; KV values/JSON documents 1 MiB; files/audio 5 MiB, video 20 MiB; sites 20 MiB total, 200 files, 5 MiB per file; requests 25 MiB. Read current values from `GET https://brewpage.app/api/limits` (MCP `get_limits`). TTL defaults to 15 days; ordinary maximum 30 days, with owner-specific caps and possible eligible automatic extensions. Treat returned expiresAt and API validation as authoritative. SDK/CLI modules are proposals, not released clients.

The repository contract/docs license is Apache-2.0; the independently packaged MCP server is MIT. The backend platform remains proprietary.
